name: Sesk in the cage
why: the game's start and all of MN04 until its ending: Sesk stands inside Skyrim's long metal cage at the camp's west edge, its door Novice-locked, the key on Jeeta-Sakka at the longhouse fire with the other guards; the cage opened, the key lifted or the guards killed are the player's doing in play, not a state of the place

name: Sesk gone (MN04 ending)
why: MN04's e-sent (Weeltul has told the player of the rootworm) switches Sesk off here and on at Helstrom's city landing: the cage stands empty at the west edge; the guards stay at the fire if alive. If Sesk died before she spoke (e-sesk-dead) her body is where she fell, which play leaves, not a state

name: The longhouse the player's (MN19 Give)
why: MN19's Give ending (after MN04, so Sesk is long gone) gives the player the longhouse and its cellar as a stronghold (giveHome): the same longhouse up the Xanmeer steps, its door and both rooms now the player's
